question: Should OpenClaw support installation of ClawHub-resolved skills.sh entries that remain explicitly unscanned, using `skills-sh:owner/repo/slug` as the permanent public contract?
rationale: This is an intentional product and supply-chain boundary decision: tests can prove the client preserves a trust label, but they cannot decide whether allowing installation under that label is an acceptable long-term trust model.

options.title: Approve the constrained external path
options.body: Approve the colon grammar and unscanned-install model after reviewing the ClawHub resolver contract and requiring the rebase-head lifecycle proof.

options.title: Require a stricter trust gate
options.body: Keep discovery and provenance support but require a different user acknowledgment or block installation until the entry is scanned.

options.title: Defer external catalog installs
options.body: Do not merge this feature now and continue supporting only native ClawHub, direct Git, and local skill installs.

recommendation.title: Approve the constrained external path
recommendation.body: Approve the colon grammar and unscanned-install model after reviewing the ClawHub resolver contract and requiring the rebase-head lifecycle proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The available evidence identifies this contributor as the current implementation contact, but a repository Skills/ClawHub owner should make the actual contract decision.
